html:
In 2015 the governor of Puerto Rico said that the island's debt of over 70 billion dollars could not be paid. It led to the largest bankruptcy of a public body in US history.

The debt had grown over years of deficits, as factories closed after the end of the tax breaks behind Operation Bootstrap and as people left. As a territory, Puerto Rico could not use the normal bankruptcy law.

In 2016 the US Congress passed PROMESA, which set up a federal oversight board with power over the island's budget. Many Puerto Ricans called it colonial rule. Cuts to schools and pensions followed, and Hurricane Maria in 2017 deepened the crisis. Mass protests in 2019 forced Governor Ricardo Rossello to resign. The government left bankruptcy in 2022, after a wave of migration.
sum: In 2015 the governor of Puerto Rico said that the island's debt of over 70 billion dollars could not be paid. It led to the largest bankruptcy of a public body in US history.
